changes.reason: THE-OWNERLESS-ACCOUNT: the new owner-assignment route can hand a service account to another org_admin, and the agent-communication same-owner rule was judged against the owner of record when a live authorization was created (issuance re-checks it), so moving the owner underneath a live session would strand it. The rule pins the refusal — 409 conflict, stable reason agent_communication_authorization_active, nothing written — for BOTH participants, pins that an account no live authorization names transfers normally, and pins that the same transfer lands once the owner revokes. Its guard is the real repository predicate over a live authorization, not a boolean stub; mutation red-proved (the guard neutralized turned the 409 into a 200 that reported result transferred)

THE-OWNERLESS-ACCOUNT closes the AUTH-503 straggler AYGHU measured and parked: ServiceAccountService.GetForActor and LookupForClient both mapped ANY store error to not-found, so a database outage read as 'no such service account' on the admin surface and as unauthorized_client at the token endpoint — verdicts the server had not reached. Both now answer AUTH-503 (503 + correlation id + ERROR log) while a genuine absence still answers not-found; IssueClientCredentials propagates the store class instead of collapsing it. Mutation red-proved twice, once per collapse point
